title: Grateful Dead Live at P.N.E. Coliseum on 1973-06-22

ai_review.summary: Hunter Seamons' matrix delivers crystal‑clear sound of a legendary 1973 Vancouver show, highlighted by an epic China > Rider and transcendent Bird Song.
ai_review.review: The recording is widely praised as an “excellent” matrix that blends Charlie Miller’s tape with Hunter Seamons’ meticulous mixing to give superb clarity, separation and a touch of audience ambience.  Musically the concert is described as near‑perfect – long, flowing sets filled with standout moments such as China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider, a 13‑minute Here Comes Sunshine, an unforgettable Bird Song, and a soaring Wharf Rat.  Reviewers are overwhelmingly enthusiastic, noting tight interplay, stellar solos and the band’s high energy throughout.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 25 detailed 5‑star reviews praise both performance and sound; only a few isolated negative comments exist, yielding an overall rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, well‑balanced mix with superb instrument separation; audience ambience adds depth without muddying the sound.  A minority note that MTX can feel “weird” compared to pure SBD tape, but overall clarity and dynamic range are praised.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Long, expansive sets with seamless transitions; the show builds beautifully from energetic openings to deep, exploratory jams, delivering a satisfying arc that keeps listeners engaged from start to finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his soaring Strat lead on China Cat, powerful vocals on Bird Song, and overall guitar tone that “rips through”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for “phil bombs aplenty” and a bass performance described as spectacular, explosive and uniquely phrased throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for an exceptional solo in China Cat (called the only truly great Weir solo) and solid rhythm work.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano solo on ‘The Race Is On’ is mentioned positively; otherwise keyboards receive general praise for adding texture.
